decision: RECOVERY_AUTHORITY = wal_triad_bridge fail-closed IN_DOUBT retention; wal.lisp start-of-recovery ABORT resolution is a violation pending repair
adopted_rule: PREPARED transactions are never resolved by assumption at recovery start. Unresolved transactions stay IN_DOUBT — isolated, never canonical, never in the replay set — until an explicit resolution frame (COMMITTED or ABORTED) arrives.

adjudication.rationale: CON-INV-07 forbids guessing an IN_DOUBT outcome. The bridge encodes exactly that invariant (fail-closed, IN_DOUBT isolated, never canonical); wal.lisp encodes the opposite (ABORT by assumption). The design claim is the norm; the bridge satisfies it, so the norm-claim-consistent surface is adopted as authority. Implementation != adoption: wal.lisp behaviour is rejected because ratifying it would ratify the assumption the norm forbids.
rejected_alternatives: adopt wal.lisp ABORT-on-recovery as the norm (rejected: violates CON-INV-07; ratifies an unadopted implementation-defined behaviour)
keep both surfaces unranked (rejected: leaves authority_conflict STOP active and classification frozen)
risks: tests/test_cae_e2e.py asserts the opposite behaviour and will fail until reconciled
wal.lisp lineage consumers may rely on ABORT-on-recovery

classification_effects.reason: CON-INV-07 adopted as governing recovery norm; bridge satisfies it; wal.lisp recorded as violation pending repair

sequenced_actions: re-classify code#03 vs code#05 under adopted authority
repair wal.lisp recovery to preserve IN_DOUBT instead of ABORT-by-assumption
re-run crash-recovery test against adopted rule

decision: WAL_TAIL_POLICY = quarantine (preserve partial tail records, exclude from canonical replay); truncation forbidden without an explicitly adopted norm plus recorded evidence
adopted_rule: Incomplete records at recovery are quarantined, never truncated. Truncation requires an explicitly adopted storage norm and recorded evidence; the existing truncation behaviour is a violation pending repair.

adjudication.rationale: The design claim forbids truncation without an explicit storage norm and the chapter declares Storage Contract and WAL Tail Policy unresolved. Adopting quarantine preserves append-only semantics and keeps the design norm governing; adopting truncation would ratify implementation-defined behaviour that the corpus itself prohibits (AGENTS.md constraints 4/5: unsupported meaning must not be silently invented).
rejected_alternatives: adopt truncate-on-recovery as the storage norm (rejected: would ratify code behaviour against an unresolved design norm; test asserts it but test != adoption)
leave tail policy unadopted (rejected: ROOT-002 stays blocked and dependent claims unclassifiable)
risks: tests/test_cae_e2e.py asserts truncation as expected and diverges from the adopted norm

adjudication.rationale: The chapter declares the durability definition unresolved; code#01 defines it as fdatasync success and the semantic join shows the same condition and same effect as the linearization-point claim. Adopting the fdatasync definition gives the promotable claim an adopted norm; the Canonical-History half of the txid-precedence claim has no implementation surface, so it is restricted rather than violated — the structural gap stays reported, not guessed.

decision: PRECEDENCE RULE = wal_triad_bridge is canonical authority for transaction/state semantics; runtime/phase-d/wal.lisp is a legacy physical WAL surface, non-authoritative for canonical state until aligned with ADR-001/ADR-002
adopted_rule: When implementation surfaces diverge on the same state semantics, the fail-closed bridge is authoritative. The wal.lisp recovery path is legacy and non-authoritative until repaired to the adopted norms.

adjudication.rationale: Two surfaces encode opposite recovery rules with no precedence rule and no adoption record; the authority_conflict STOP cannot lift without adjudication. The bridge is fail-closed and matches the adopted norms of ADR-001/ADR-002/ADR-003; wal.lisp matches none of them, so precedence follows the adopted norms. The divergent-node claim retains keyword-level-only evidence, so its status is restricted, not VERIFIED.
rejected_alternatives: declare wal.lisp authoritative (rejected: contradicts all adopted norms)
freeze classification indefinitely (rejected: STOP condition stays active; adjudication is the only path named in causal_resolution)
risks: two surfaces continue to exist; divergence is reported, not deleted
restriction statuses are authority-scope facts, not semantic proofs
